clue.text: Room to include pious article by a public school boy

indicators.note: the room is said to take in the next pieces, so they go inside it

parts.note: a salon is a reception room
PI is an old abbreviation for pious, devout
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A school pupil is given a room alongside a devout piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' puts PI and A inside SALON, between its O and N. Shrewsbury School, an old English public (private) school, calls its pupils Salopians, from Salop, an old name for Shropshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils of Shrewsbury School are known by this name, taken from the Latin-derived name of their county.

clue.text: A Western heroine

parts.note: reads as the leading lady of a cowboy film, but means a woman surnamed Western who is a novel's heroine

explanation.walkthrough: In Fielding's novel Tom Jones the heroine is Sophia Western, daughter of Squire Western; 'Western' looks like the film genre.
explanation.definitionFit: The beloved of Tom Jones in Fielding's novel bears the family name Western.

clue.text: Surgeon who lent an ear?

explanation.surface: A doctor who once listened to someone's troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Lister pioneered antiseptic surgery; the second reading takes the answer as 'one who listens'.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Lister was the Victorian pioneer of antiseptic operations, and one who listens is, by a made-up word, a listener.

clue.text: Main forwarding agent

parts.note: reads as a shipping firm's chief agent, but 'main' is the sea and the agent is the thing that drives a vessel forward through it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is an old word for the open sea, so the agent forwarding a ship on the main is its screw.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's screw drives it forward through the sea, the 'main' of old sea songs.

clue.text: A crushed lime before speech leads to improvement

indicators.note: something crushed is broken up and reshaped, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: Crushing a lime before giving a talk makes things better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crushed' rearranges LIME into MELI, which follows A; 'before' and 'leads to' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Making something better is the meaning of this formal word, from Latin melior, better.

clue.text: Father's after the girl, that's plain

indicators.note: Father's comes after the girl, so it goes second

parts.note: Pam is a girl's name
Pa is father, and with 's added it gives PAS

explanation.surface: Dad is following his daughter around; that much is obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' looks like the adjective 'obvious' but is the noun, a stretch of flat land.
explanation.definitionFit: The vast treeless grasslands of Argentina form a great flat expanse.

clue.text: Deck gives trouble to the Navy

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A ship's deck causes problems for the sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' is the verb, to decorate, not part of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck something, as with holly, is to decorate it.

clue.text: Earned for work over the bar

definitions.text: Earned for work over the bar

parts.words: Earned for work over the bar
parts.note: reads as a barman's wages, but the bar is a sandbank at a harbour mouth and the work is steering ships across it

explanation.walkthrough: The 'bar' is a sandbar across a harbour entrance; the fee a pilot earns for guiding a ship over it has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The charge made by a harbour pilot for guiding a vessel in is named after his job.

clue.text: Spaniel's bound to identify it ?

parts.note: reads as a dog being sure to name something, but 'bound' is a leap: the spaniel's leap gives the breed its name

explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' is a jump, not 'certain': this breed of spaniel is named for springing at game to flush it.
explanation.definitionFit: This breed of spaniel takes its name from leaping to flush birds from cover.

clue.text: Ignore the feast ?

explanation.surface: Someone is told to skip the banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'pass over' something is to ignore it; written as one word it is the Jewish festival.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass someone over is to overlook them, and the spring Jewish festival marks the Exodus from Egypt.

clue.text: Bad mistake made by woman about bird

indicators.note: the woman's word goes around the bird, enclosing it

parts.note: her is a word for a woman
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A woman is blamed for a blunder concerning a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts OWL inside HER.
explanation.definitionFit: A glaring blunder, especially a laughable one, is called this.

clue.text: Gateshead boys began to collect the luggage

parts.note: read as Gate's head, the first letter of gate
lads are boys

indicators.note: to collect is to gather up, so the letters are gathered into a new order

explanation.surface: Lads from Gateshead, a town in north-east England, start gathering the bags.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead, a town on the Tyne, is split as 'Gate's head', giving G; 'collect' rearranges BEGAN TO into TONEBAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged leather travelling case, named after the Victorian prime minister, is a piece of luggage.

clue.text: It was Johnson's tragedy, being in dire need

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Samuel Johnson's tragic play arose when he was desperately short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the run IRENE inside 'dIRE NEed'. Samuel Johnson wrote a verse tragedy of this name, staged in 1749.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Johnson's only play, a blank-verse tragedy, carried this title.

clue.text: It's in London I drink to capacity

parts.note: a sling is a cocktail, as in Singapore sling
a ton is a measure of a ship's carrying capacity

explanation.surface: A Londoner says he drinks until he is full.
explanation.walkthrough: Islington is a borough of north London; a ton is a unit of a ship's cargo capacity.
explanation.definitionFit: This north London borough is a district within the capital.

clue.text: Pickwickian reads Tennyson verse ?

parts.note: the poet's first name was Alfred
a jingle is light rhyming verse

explanation.surface: A character from Dickens recites some of Tennyson's poems.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfred Jingle is the glib strolling actor in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers; 'reads' just joins definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: This fast-talking rogue is one of the characters in Dickens's Pickwick Papers.

clue.text: Cavalry club teams

parts.note: an iron is a golf club
sides are teams

explanation.surface: Mounted soldiers form teams at their club.
explanation.walkthrough: Cromwell's cavalry in the English Civil War were nicknamed Ironsides.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Cromwell's horse soldiers in the Civil War were given this nickname.

clue.text: He kills the animals in the end

parts.note: an ass is a donkey, an animal
ass is slang for the backside, the rear end
taken as written

explanation.surface: A murderer finishes off the creatures at last.
explanation.walkthrough: The animal ASS and the rear-end ASS sit side by side, then IN follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A murderer, especially of a public figure, is one who kills.

clue.text: At last these tributes are likely to be cut

definitions.text: At last these tributes are likely to be cut

parts.words: At last these tributes are likely to be cut
parts.note: reads as praise being trimmed, but the tributes come at the very end of life and are cut into stone

explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' means carved, not reduced: these final tributes are inscribed on gravestones.
explanation.definitionFit: Inscriptions on tombs honour the dead, so they are final tributes carved in stone.

clue.text: Unfounded belief of poet in U.S.S.R. — it needs altering

indicators.note: the letters need changing round, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poet in the Soviet Union holds an irrational idea that needs revising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altering' rearranges the twelve letters of POET IN USSR IT; 'needs' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A baseless belief in luck or omens is irrational credulity.

clue.text: Current is soft in a lake ?

indicators.note: the soft sign goes inside the lake

parts.note: a mere is a lake
p (piano) means soft in music

explanation.surface: A stream runs gently into a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts P inside MERE, after A. The definition is by example: the ampere is the unit of electric current, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The SI unit of electric current measures its flow.

clue.text: Fast to 1.50--then a vegetable

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
in Roman numerals I is one and L is fifty

explanation.surface: Someone fasts until ten to two, then eats some greens.
explanation.walkthrough: '1.50' looks like a time, ten to two, but is the Roman numerals I and L.
explanation.definitionFit: This edible pulse is a legume, eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Time for tea — or lotos-eating ?

explanation.surface: Teatime, or a lazy idle day.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson's The Lotos-Eaters describes 'a land In which it seemed always afternoon'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is taken in the hours after midday, and Tennyson's lotos-eaters lived where that time of day seemed to last for ever.

clue.text: Patron doesn't include music

indicators.note: the words are said to contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: A patron of the arts refuses to put music in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'include' marks RONDO inside 'patRON DOesn't'.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of music with a recurring main theme, often a sonata finale, has this name.

clue.text: A thousand enter part of the battle

indicators.note: the thousand goes into the other word

parts.note: some means a part of
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A thousand soldiers join one part of the fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enter' puts M inside SOME; the battle is the 1916 Somme.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1916 offensive on the Western Front was named after the river in northern France.

clue.text: Wood follows us back, being indolent

indicators.note: the wood comes after the other piece
us is read backwards, from back to front

parts.note: taken as written
pine is a wood

explanation.surface: A forest trails behind us, and we are lazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns US into SU, and 'follows' puts PINE after it; 'being' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying flat on one's back suggests inactivity, so the word also means lazy.

clue.text: Given an order, possibly I tend to be dutiful

parts.note: OBE is the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Once honoured with a medal, someone resolves to do their duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges I TEND into DIENT after OBE, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A dutiful person does as told, complying with orders.

clue.text: Old king gets home with gold

parts.note: a nest is a home
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: An aged monarch acquires a house along with some gold.
explanation.walkthrough: Nestor is the wise old king of Pylos in Homer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer's Iliad the aged king of Pylos is the wise counsellor of the Greeks.

clue.text: White's case is somewhat fragile

explanation.surface: A white container that breaks rather easily.
explanation.walkthrough: The white of an egg is enclosed in its shell; as an adjective the word means thin and delicate.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer casing of an egg holds its white, and the word also describes delicate, brittle things like fine china.
